claim_or_location: All query predicted_lineage labels come from a 'frozen' scANVI classifier (freeze_classifier=True); Braun collapses to astrocyte (97.8 %), Siletti false-malignant 0.000, LaBelle/Liu T cells 0.000 recovered
evidence: State-dict diff reference models/scanvi vs each models/scanvi_query_<q>: z_encoder identical (max |diff| 0) but classifier BatchNorm affine parameters changed (Braun: Layer0 gamma 0.99, beta 1.36; Layer1 gamma 1.14, beta 1.21; similar for all five queries). Cause: scvi-tools 1.4.2 _archesmixin._set_params_online_update tests `'.0.' in key`, which matches the module prefix 'classifier.classifier.0.' and sets requires_grad=True on every classifier parameter; gradient hooks are only attached to nn.Linear weights, so the BN gamma/beta of the classifier train under the unlabelled scANVI loss. Verified live: SCANVI.load_query_data(filbin) shows classifier 'Layer 0.1.weight/bias' and 'Layer 1.1.weight/bias' requires_grad=True. Applying the reference classifier (reference state dict) to the saved, identical query latents: Braun 82,910/100,000 malignant, 13,137 neuron (saved: 97,822 astrocyte, 0 malignant); expected-lineage recovery 0.259 vs 0.035; Siletti 3,541 malignant (3.5 %, 3,360 of them OPCs) vs 0; LaBelle author T cells -> T_NK 0.559 vs 0.000 (immune agreement 0.923 vs 0.827); Liu T cell 0.333 vs 0.000, Liu normal->match 0.800 vs 0.747, Liu neuron 1,182 vs 116, Liu author-malignant->malignant 0.956 vs 0.993. The per-query classifier reproduces the saved labels 100 %, the untrained surgery model reproduces my reference-classifier labels 100 % (Filbin).
impact_on_conclusions: predicted_lineage, scanvi_maxprob/uncertainty_prob and scanvi_probs in query_mapping.h5ad, mapping_summary.csv, mapping_<q>_author_vs_predicted.csv, mapping_normal_reference_specificity.csv, mapping_author_agreement.json, malignant_fraction_scanvi for queries in atlas_v1_summary.csv, both phase5 figures, notes §2-5 and the README 'known limitations' describe five different, unintentionally re-fitted classifiers. The headline Braun 'astrocyte collapse', the '0 false-malignant on Siletti' and the 'T-cell failure of the frozen classifier' are artifacts; with the actual reference classifier fetal progenitors are called malignant (consistent with the notes' own 0-epoch sensitivity run) and T cells are partly recovered.
recommendation: Regenerate query predictions with the reference classifier (apply models/scanvi classifier to the saved latents, or load_query_data without training / set requires_grad=False on classifier.* before train), re-derive all mapping tables, figures and notes §2-5; report the scvi-tools behaviour as a caveat; keep knn_lineage as the primary label.

claim_or_location: Queries are 'mapped by scArches/scANVI surgery' in which 'only the weights attached to new categories receive non-zero gradients'
evidence: Reference scANVI was built with scvi-tools defaults: encode_covariates absent from init_params_ (False), use_batch_norm 'both', no layer norm; z_encoder.encoder.n_cat_list == [] so the encoder receives no batch/study/assay input and the online-update hook zeroes its whole gradient. Encoder state identical before/after 100 epochs for all five queries. Untrained load_query_data latent for Filbin equals the saved post-training latent (max |diff| 0.0039 = float16 rounding; r = 1.000000). Hence X_scanvi for every query is the zero-shot output of the reference encoder; the 41 min of CPU training changed only decoder first-layer columns, decoder BN and (IM-01) classifier BN.
impact_on_conclusions: No query batch effect is removed in latent space; the kNN uncertainty ~1.0 for all Smart-seq2/TPM cohorts and 0.985 for Braun partly measures uncorrected protocol shift, not biology. The notes' sensitivity statement (distance 2.60 untrained vs 2.66 trained) is explained: nothing can change. The description 'scArches surgery' over-states the method; the plan's 'fine-tune with frozen reference weights' was not achievable with this reference configuration.
recommendation: Describe Phase 5 as zero-shot encoder projection; if adaptive mapping is wanted retrain the reference with encode_covariates=True (scArches-recommended: layer norm, no batch norm) and re-run; drop the 100-epoch training otherwise (it only introduces IM-01).

claim_or_location: scANVI agreement with lineage_label on the 220,309 labelled cells 0.987; per-class recall astrocyte 0.815, T_NK 0.467
evidence: Recomputed from predicted_labels.txt: 0.9873 (match). attr_dict train_indices_/validation_indices_ (random 90/10 cell split): labelled train 198,279 cells accuracy 0.9881; labelled validation 22,030 cells accuracy 0.9804; validation recall astrocyte 0.663, T_NK 0.388, oligodendrocyte 0.904, vascular 0.928, neuron 0.958, malignant 0.998. history: validation_accuracy peaks 0.986 at epoch 8 and falls to 0.977 at epoch 24 while validation_classification_loss rises 0.048 -> 0.095 and train_accuracy climbs to 0.995 (no early stopping; 25 fixed epochs). Split is by cell, not by sample/patient.
impact_on_conclusions: The 0.987 is 90 % training-set accuracy and the per-class recalls for the small classes are over-stated by 0.08-0.15; the classifier was still over-fitting when training stopped. No patient-held-out estimate exists, so generalisation to new tumours is unmeasured.
recommendation: Report held-out (validation) accuracy and per-class recall; add patient-grouped cross-validation; select epochs by validation classification loss or use early stopping on it.

claim_or_location: scVI covariates: batch = sample_id with categorical covariates study and assay
evidence: Every sample_id belongs to exactly one study and one assay (0 sample_ids span two studies; sample ids are study-prefixed, e.g. jessa_scrna__P-1764_S-1766 vs jessa_multiome__P-1764_S-1766). The study/assay one-hots are therefore linear functions of the batch one-hot and add no information to the decoder; the design is over-parameterised (rank-deficient), not harmful. With encode_covariates=False none of these enter the encoder (see IM-02). In query mapping each query adds redundant new study/assay/sample columns.
impact_on_conclusions: No effect on the reference embedding; the notes should not imply separate correction for study and assay. Cross-assay anchoring relies on the 4 Jessa patients profiled by both scRNA and multiome and on shared biology, not on the covariates.
recommendation: Drop study/assay covariates or document that they are nested in sample_id; if assay correction matters, consider study/assay as batch with sample as covariate, or encode_covariates=True.
